title: Stale story-042 per-client-reserve NatSpec on setAsideBufferSize contradicts story-047 global-recipient behaviour — conflicting spec sources inside the same file
specText: story-047 (commit 933620d): "rework _distributeBuffer() to single aggregate transfer to recipient" vs stale NatSpec: "this percentage of the client's own realized surplus is returned to the client instead of going to `recipient`, giving the client a reserve to absorb below-par dips" (AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53) and "percentage of the client's realized surplus is returned to the client (a reserve against ...)" (IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132)
specSource: git commit 933620d body vs src/AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 and src/interfaces/IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132
actualBehavior: Since story-047, the set-aside is NEVER returned to the client; it is summed across all clients and sent in one transfer to the global setAsideBufferRecipient (ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:323, ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:368). The setAsideBufferSize NatSpec in both AYieldStrategy and IYieldStrategy still promises the superseded story-042 per-client return semantics, directly contradicting the (correct) new NatSpec on setAsideBufferRecipient three lines below it. An integrator reading setAsideBufferSize docs would wrongly conclude their contract receives its own buffer back.
deviation: Stale story-042 NatSpec contradicts story-047 behaviour — the spec sources conflict inside the same file.
impact: Pure documentation deviation; no code-behaviour security impact. The behaviour leg (multi-client cross-subsidy footgun the stale docs set up) is carried by L-15.
recommendation: Update AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 and IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132 to state the percentage is routed to setAsideBufferRecipient (protocol-level yield routing, not a client reserve). qa-bundler emits ONE combined doc-fix item with L-15's NatSpec leg, not two parallel items.
report: spec-conformance.md (Law-2 faithfulness; NOT the QA bundle — doc-fix leg merged with L-15 in the QA bundle)
